content.text:
So two big questions that came up discussing this with leadership and everything. It sounds like they're on board and ready to have the contract written up and sent over. A couple of things were... One, let's say it's November and December, and we're noticing that something's not going right the way that it had been working. Or I just... A little bit off. Who would be servicing that?
How would we be able to reach out for support?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
So just to make sure I'm understanding you, you're saying once everything's stood up, if something's not quite working properly... I guess there are probably two points there, but yes. So from our side, if it's functionality on the Mulesoft platform that we've said Mulesoft has like the ability to connect the pack load... I don't know why I can't say that name to sales. Salesforce, right?
If we can't do that, there's language in the Salesforce contract. Or you can just rip it up, and then on the implementation side, I'll... Kailash, answer.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
So when then? Once the whole system is set up, then ideally it should work. But considering, as you mentioned, if there is a huge volume or rush that impacts the system, then I think there are two ways. One, we offer managed services that can help you on a monthly basis so that the team will be available to you to support for a fixed number of hours, and then any changes in anything required, we will be able to offer that.
That is one of the services that we do provide. There is no contract or there is no minimum duration of time. You can just let us know a month in advance and then we can get started on that.
So we do provide those services and then I can get a price to you on that. On how effectively we can give you a good price on it.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: We can send you the language that Sam's referencing in the MSA. It's basically called the warranties clause that anything that we represent would work during the sales cycle. Will it actually work?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Okay, perfect. Just like even a couple of reports that we had set up to our main dashboards like that for like a week weren't working. And then we were able to figure it out that our Microft exchange account had updated and we just have to update.
And Salesforce. So it was like something simple like that where we just were like, hey, what if something with pack updates or something with soft updates and now they're not completely compatible and something's just a little bit off? We just want to make sure that we're still taking care of there. Perfect.
And then the other thing was speaking with Nick at the Spokane Indians, it sounds like they are open to it and kind of wanted to like talk further about it and kind of see how it works for us. So our leadership team was wondering because I know like in the last PF you sent over, it was contingent on them signing up in June as well. Is if we sign up for the no discount just Chiefs and then come October when they're out of their season doing budget stuff and they sign up. Is there any way that we could do like a the two part payment plans and quarterly just do like half upfront and then if they do end up signing up, just taking that second part with a discount. Or does both teams have to sign when we sign in June?

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
No, I think I can respond to that. I think that's reasonable. The one thing we wouldn't be able to do is after you guys sign, then, assuming all the software works, everything's good, rip up that contract and be like, "Here's the exact same thing, but for cheaper."
But what we could do is because you guys are already customers on the discounted pricing that was shared for the additional contract, and that's something that Sam could just send in writing like he's your account executive for both accounts all year.
So assuming that happens within this fiscal year.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Okay, perfect. Just talking over with them. They're obviously in the middle of their season, so like, "Hey, this is great, but this is definitely an off-season." Even their fiscal year is January 1st, whereas ours is July 1st.
So even they're on a different timeline than us. They're like, "Hey, we can't put this into this year," so we're like, "Okay, well, what would that look like?" So that makes total sense. Fair.

content.text: From the implementation point of view, I think we need to do a tech discovery with them to analyze what would be needed to build upon and what would be the timeline and investment from their side or the implementation part of it.

content.text: Okay, sure.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Does this mean that you guys are comfortable with the other side of the contract or...? And like the approvals are in place. Where do you guys stand on everything now?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
So we pitched it to our team president and BP, they've signed off on it and how we update the budget numbers, including this. Now it's just waiting on one approval from our CEO. He's looked over the information and looked everything over.
So, he hasn't been in the office all day today. I think he's in later this week. But if we have something to have them sign and look over, it sounds like at least we got the majority approval that we needed at this point.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Okay, awesome. That's great news. You said you thought that he was back in the office. Is he signing or who would be signing?

content.text: Typically going to be me signing or Vijay probably signing in one of those two. So we just need... I'll send it over to give us the formal thumbs up. But it's real close there. content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
You read my mind. I was going to say... I'm sure you want to look at what the language looks like either way. So Sam can publish that directly to you for signature. Then... Yeah, once you guys have that conversation, if it's a yes, you could just sign it. Do you foresee any pushback or considering that you got two out of three yeses, you think it's going to be an easy yes?
How do these combos usually go?

content.speaker: Speaker 5
content.text:
Yeah, I think we've done already the hardest in the room. So I think for us now, it's just he's going to look at it in the totality of... He's the CEO of both teams, so he'll look at it from the bigger scope there.
But he's the one that's really going to care about the manner if he says yes. I mean, the Indians are most likely going to get it as well, too. So, he's just kind of the last formal. Yes, we need to get from.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Okay, awesome. Well, we'll send that over. Do you guys...? Two questions. 1, assuming he is in the office tomorrow. This is mostly just for me to report up the chain so we have somebody ready to countersign. Do you think it's reasonable to have this signed by Wednesday or is that crazy?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Probably estimate more Thursday or Friday just because he's not in today, and if he wants to have a day or two to look it over, I'd probably... A more closer to Thursday.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Okay, good deal. That's why I asked. Perfect. Do you mind if we just block off a last fifteen-minute sink on Thursday just in case any questions do come up? It's like, "We're good, we're covered, we can hop on, we can talk about it." What times work best for you guys?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Any time after 01:00 pm on Thursday would work.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Sam, you want to do five Eastern again?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Let's do that.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: All right. Okay. So we owe you guys the... Sign with the formal contract and the warranties clause from the MSA so you guys can look over that. Then cash... Did you have anything you were going to send?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Yeah. I'll send out the SW as well. Then you guys can review and sign. Thanks for calling.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: On then?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Just one final confirmation July 15 start date and quarterly billing that that's still what you guys are looking for.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: I think just splitting it into half. So do July 15 and then January 15. Okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: For the invoices, you're saying correct? Okay, so semi-annual and SE quarterly.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Our accountant has to send in or pay an invoice worth...

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Our billing team is going to say that sounds better, so good.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: All right. Awesome. I think we can get to work on getting you guys those last few items and then we'll move the call out to Thursday. Any other questions from you all?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Side before we...

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: We break here? Well, we're looking forward to getting this one kicked off, guys. Thank you.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Thank you, Sam.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Thanks, guys. Bye.
